method.label: Color the groups forced by symmetry

annotationRationale: Reflection and rotation symmetry force equal colors within each group of squares. The multiplication principle counts the independent color choices for the ten groups.
sourceMethod: Follows the second official solution, grouping squares by their rotation and reflection orbits. Coordinate representatives replace the absent labeled solution diagram and justify the count of ten groups.

review.mathCheck: Signed coordinate swaps give exactly the ten representatives \(0\le v\le u\le3\). Their groups cover all 49 cells: one group of size 1, six of size 4, and three of size 8. Independent binary coloring gives \(2^{10}-2=1022\), choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA Q20's orbit method on page 10. The coordinate representatives replace the figure's ten labels A through J and justify both completeness and independence.
review.annotationCheck: All three assessed nodes contribute directly. The explanation proves that the groups are distinct and exhaustive, that their colorings satisfy every required symmetry, and that exactly two colorings are excluded.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact reflection, rotation, and multiplication-principle links cover the named steps. The ten-group classification combines these skills; those links alone do not represent a separate national orbit-counting standard.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: G-CO.A.3 supports square self-symmetries. The accepted narrower/partial G-CO.A.4 and G-CO.A.2 links support transformation definitions and coordinate action only. This problem does not demonstrate general definition development, translations, or comparisons with nonisometries. No US counting link is supplied.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: cnm_131 and cnm_244 appropriately assess symmetry constraints; cnm_h231 assesses the ten independent color choices. The elementary coordinate argument supplies the grouping method without requiring group theory.
